sub_areas.name: Beamsville
sub_areas.note: The town's administrative and commercial centre, on the south shore of Lake Ontario with a QEW interchange (Wikipedia, 43.1658 N 79.4764 W). OGS point queries at the Wikipedia coordinate and at the reference coordinate (43.16, -79.48) both return clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Queenston Formation; a lakeshore point north of the QEW (43.1855, -79.5181) returns Paleozoic bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) over Queenston.

sub_areas.name: Vineland
sub_areas.note: Second-largest community, bordered by Twenty Mile Creek and Jordan to the east, Lake Ontario to the north, Beamsville to the west; commercial centre along King Street (Wikipedia, 43.1539 N 79.3922 W). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate returns coarse-textured glaciolacustrine sand and gravel (unit 9) over Queenston Formation; a point on the village's west side (43.1494, -79.4037) returns clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Queenston.

sub_areas.name: Vineland Station
sub_areas.note: Hamlet north of Vineland near the lake (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, 43.1915 N 79.3952 W); the ECCC Vineland Station RCS climate station sits here. OGS point query returns clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: Jordan
sub_areas.note: On the eastern edge of the town, bordered by Twenty Mile Creek and Vineland to the west, Lake Ontario to the north, St. Catharines to the east and Pelham to the south (Wikipedia, 43.1333 N 79.35 W). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate returns clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Queenston Formation; a point in the village at 43.1483, -79.3703 also returns unit 5d over Queenston.

sub_areas.name: Jordan Station
sub_areas.note: Hamlet at the Twenty Mile Creek harbour; Jordan and Jordan Station were historically shipping centres at the mouth of the Twenty (Wikipedia). OpenStreetMap Nominatim coordinate 43.1636 N 79.3604 W. OGS point queries here and at 43.1710, -79.3663 both return coarse-textured glaciolacustrine sand and gravel (unit 9) over Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: Campden
sub_areas.note: Hamlet south of Beamsville toward the escarpment (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, 43.1352 N 79.4333 W; Wikipedia lists it among the town's communities). OGS point query returns clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Lockport Formation dolostone (Silurian), i.e. above the Queenston/Lockport contact. A point farther south at 43.1224, -79.4419 returns fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay (unit 8a) over Lockport.

sub_areas.name: Escarpment brow (between Beamsville and Vineland)
sub_areas.note: The Wikipedia article coordinate for Lincoln (43.1528 N 79.4183 W) falls on the Niagara Escarpment; OGS point query returns Paleozoic bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) over Lockport Formation (Goat Island, Gasport, Vinemount members). Wikipedia: the town lies between the south shore of Lake Ontario and the Niagara Escarpment; Rockway and Tintern are the town's other listed communities (not queried).

surficial.description: Clay to silt-textured till (derived from glaciolacustrine deposits or shale). Regional literature calls the below-escarpment till of this area Halton Till; that name is not carried in the OGS layer attributes and was not verified here.
surficial.where: Most of the Iroquois plain below the escarpment: query points at the reference coordinate (43.16, -79.48), Beamsville (43.1658, -79.4764), west Vineland (43.1494, -79.4037), Vineland Station (43.1915, -79.3952), Jordan (43.1333, -79.35 and 43.1483, -79.3703) and Campden (43.1352, -79.4333) all return unit 5d.

surficial.unit: OGS MRD128-REV unit 9 - Coarse-textured glaciolacustrine deposits
surficial.description: Sand, gravel, minor silt and clay (former glacial Lake Iroquois nearshore and beach deposits).
surficial.where: Twenty Mile Creek mouth and lower valley: query points at Jordan Station (43.1636, -79.3604 and 43.1710, -79.3663) and Vineland village (43.1539, -79.3922) return unit 9.

surficial.description: Bedrock at or near surface (drift too thin to map).
surficial.where: Escarpment brow between Beamsville and Vineland (43.1528, -79.4183, over Lockport dolostone) and a lakeshore point north of the QEW at Beamsville (43.1855, -79.5181, over Queenston shale).

surficial.unit: OGS MRD128-REV unit 8a - Fine-textured glaciolacustrine deposits
surficial.description: Silt and clay, minor sand and gravel; massive to well laminated.
surficial.where: Plateau above the escarpment south of Campden and Vineland: query points at 43.1224, -79.4419 and 43.1090, -79.3925 return unit 8a over Lockport Formation.

bedrock.formation: Queenston Formation (Upper Ordovician red shale) below the Niagara Escarpment; Lockport Formation (Silurian dolostone) on and above the escarpment (OGS MRD219).
bedrock.description: Queenston: red shale and siltstone, minor green shale and siltstone, and variable calcareous siltstone to sandstone and limestone interbeds; returned at the reference coordinate, Beamsville, Vineland, Vineland Station, Jordan and Jordan Station. Lockport: thick-bedded blue-grey crinoidal limestone to dolostone (Gasport Mb), light brown locally cherty dolostone (Goat Island Mb), argillaceous dolostone and shale (Vinemount shale beds) and bituminous dark brown dolostone (Eramosa Mb); returned at Campden, the escarpment brow and the plateau points. The OGS bedrock layer skips the thin intervening Clinton and Cataract group units at this map scale; the contact between Queenston and Lockport polygons runs along the escarpment face across the south of the town.
bedrock.depth_note: Depth to bedrock was not retrieved (no drift-thickness dataset queried). OGS surficial mapping shows bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) on the escarpment brow near 43.1528, -79.4183 and at a lakeshore point north of Beamsville (43.1855, -79.5181); elsewhere Queenston shale lies beneath till or glaciolacustrine sand of unstated thickness.

implications_for_piles: Two bedrock regimes in one town: below the escarpment (Beamsville, Vineland, Jordan, Jordan Station, Vineland Station) helical piles advance through clay-silt till or lake sand toward Queenston red shale; on and above the escarpment (Campden, Rockway, Tintern area) they advance through thin till or laminated silt-clay toward Lockport dolostone, which is far harder than shale. A pile design or torque expectation from one side of the escarpment does not transfer to the other (OGS MRD128-REV and MRD219 point queries).

Near-surface bedrock (OGS unit 3) is mapped at the escarpment brow between Beamsville and Vineland and at a lakeshore point north of Beamsville; in those areas refusal at shallow depth is a site condition to confirm before installation.

The Twenty Mile Creek mouth and lower valley (Jordan Station, Vineland village) are mapped as coarse glaciolacustrine sand and gravel (unit 9) rather than till; the Iroquois plain around Beamsville is clay-to-silt till (unit 5d). Soil texture, and therefore pile capacity per turn of torque, differs between these neighbourhoods.

No Town of Lincoln deck drawing, footing-depth figure, helical-pile submission rule or CCMC/BMEC requirement was retrieved: lincoln.ca was unreachable from this environment (see permits). Do not state a Lincoln-specific footing depth or engineer requirement until that page or PDF is read.

Frost-free figures for Vineland are given only as probabilities: 50% probability of last spring frost Apr 25 and first fall frost Oct 20, and a 50% probability of a frost-free period of 179 days or less; the 179 figure above is that 50% value.
